config.text: This application provides mapping data for designated Section 368 energy corridors in 11 Western states encompassing a wide range of geospatial information pertinent to corridor routing decisions. The following animated help shows how the tools in the app works.  For a static help document or for more information about this site, click here or on the About / Help button on the top right in the app's header.
Layer List Tool

The Layer List button groups layers by subject matter, called Operational Layers.   

You can turn layers on and off and view more information about the layers.
Source Agency

The Source Agency button series groups layers by the Federal Agency responsible for the data.  You can turn layers on and off and view more information about a layer by clicking on the button displaying an agency icon.
ReST and Item Pages

To access additional information for layers,  

in the Table of Contents, click on the ellipses (...) to the right of the layer name and select Description.  This will open either the ReST page or the Item page for the layer.
Pop-Ups
Display an informative Pop-up by clicking on a feature on the map.
MLRS

The dynamic xxxx layers have an additional link to the MLRS xxxx.

Scroll to the bottom on the pop-up and click the xxx (MLRS log) to open
Important Links

About Help

This application provides mapping data for designated Section 368 energy corridors in 11 Western states encompassing a wide range of geospatial information pertinent to corridor routing decisions. A right of way authorizes specific use of public land for a specified period of time that is appropriate for the life of the project. For more information, see: https://www.blm.gov/programs/lands-and-realty/rights-way.  


Layer List 

The Layer List button groups layers by subject matter, (also called Operational Layers).  You can turn layers on and off individually or by subject matter group, toggle layer transparency, and view more information about a layer, and toggle layer labels.

Add Data 

The Add Data Widget allows you to temporarily add data sources to your map.   Don’t have data of your own?  You can search for public data by selecting “Living Atlas” from the drop-down menu and then typing in your own key words.

Select Data 

The Select Tool allows you to use a rectangle to select one or more layers and perform statistics, view in the table, or export.

Source Agency 

The Source Agency button series groups layers by the four federal agencies responsible for the majority of the data on the map.  By clicking the three ellipses to the right of a layer, you can perform a variety of activities, including:  labeling, filtering for desired attributes, performing statistics, creating tables, changing the way the layer displays, or exporting the data. 

 

BLM – Bureau of Land Management 

USFWS – United States Fish and Wildlife Serve 

NPS – National Parks Service 

USFS – United States Forest Service

Pop-up 

Display an informative Pop-up by clicking on the feature on the map.

ReST and Item Pages 

To access additional information for layers, in the Table of Contents, click on the ellipses (...) to the right of the layer name and select Description.  This will open either the ReST page or the Item page for the layer.

For more information, see: https://www.blm.gov/programs/lands-and-realty/rights-way.  

The following animated help shows how the tools in the app works.  For a static help document or for more information about this site, click here or on the About / Help button on the top right in the header.

Layer List 

The Layer List button groups layers by subject matter, (also called Operational Layers).    

You can turn layers on and off individually or by subject matter group, toggle layer transparency, and view more information about a layer, and toggle layer labels.

Add Data 

The Add Data Widget allows you to temporarily add data sources to your map.   Don’t have data of your own?   You can search for public data by selecting “Living Atlas” from the drop-down menu and then typing in your own key words.

Select Data 

The Select Tool allows you to use a rectangle to select one or more layers and perform statistics, view in the table, or export.

Source Agency 

The Source Agency button series groups layers by the four federal agencies responsible for the majority of the data on the map.  By clicking the three ellipses to the right of a layer, you can perform a variety of activities, including:  labeling, filtering for desired attributes, performing statistics, creating tables, changing the way the layer displays, or exporting the data. 

  

BLM – Bureau of Land Management 

USFWS – United States Fish and Wildlife Serve 

NPS – National Parks Service 

USFS – United States Forest Service

Pop-up 

Display an informative Pop-up by clicking on the feature on the map.

ReST and Item Pages 

To access additional information for layers, in the Table of Contents, click on the ellipses (...) to the right of the layer name and select Description.  This will open either the ReST page or the Item page for the layer.

Metadata 

Some layers (hosted features services) have additional metadata associated with them.  Scroll to the bottom of the pop-up and click the BLM logo to open the PDF metadata file.

Link to MLRS 

The four dynamic Rights-of-Way Legal Land Description layers have an additional link to the Mineral & Land Records System (MLRS).   Scroll to the bottom of the pop-up and click the MLRS logo to open access these files.

Search 

The search bar can be used for standard searches by address or place name; but, can also be used to search by name of project. Using the arrow on the left side, you can narrow which layers you want to search within.

Map Tools 

The map contains standard map tools, including: zoom, return to home, find location (available on mobile only), change basemap, measure distance and area, draw and annotate, and print.

Table 

The attribute tables of all layers can be viewed, filtered, and analyzed.  Tables can be accessed by clicking on the arrow at the bottom of the screen.
